ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information and its Enforcement Decree, Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality, Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, and the Supreme Court Regulations on Commercial Registration; UBO identification follows the 25% ownership/control standard applied by Korean financial institutions and the Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Corporate Existence of the Foreign Direct Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry, court, or Chamber of Commerce in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize before a local notary in the country of origin; then obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority for an Apostille Convention state. For a non-member state, complete notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate with jurisdiction. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Certificate of No Tax Arrears of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Revenue authority or company registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain an official certificate from the issuing authority; notarize the certificate; then apply for a Hague Apostille if the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member. For a non-member issuing state, apply for consular legalization through the Korean diplomatic mission. The two authentication paths are separate alternatives and must not be combined in one sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Korean Incorporation Agent, Registered Directors, and Representative Director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign investing company, authenticated by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the board resolution and power of attorney notarized in the country of origin; then apply for a Hague Apostille if the origin country is a Party to the Apostille Convention. If the origin country is not an Apostille member, obtain Korean consular legalization of the same document through the Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; never apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Ultimate Parent and Draft Articles of Association of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate parent company secretary or the Korean law firm preparing the incorporation filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the parent articles as true copies before a notary public; obtain a Hague Apostille where the parent jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state. For parent jurisdictions outside the Apostille Convention, obtain Korean consular legalization. The draft Korean Articles of Association must be notarized in Korea by a Korean notary public. The two paths remain separate; no sequential apostille plus consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Relationship Profile of the Foreign Investor's Principal Depository Bank, Including Source of Funds Statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank holding the foreign investor's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the bank reference letter signed by an authorized bank officer and notarized; if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille member, attach a Hague Apostille issued by the designated competent authority. For a bank in a non-member jurisdiction, the notarized letter must proceed to Korean consular legalization. The apostille and consular legalization pathways are mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be applied sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders owning 25% or more, all directors, executive officers, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean FIU domestic sanctions list, plus negative-news and politically exposed person (PEP) databases, including family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, higher-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed corporate structures, or where funding sources show unexplained complexity. Screening must occur pre-incorporation and continuously thereafter, and system hits must be independently adjudicated by the AML compliance officer and escalated to the FIU when facts indicate suspicious activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office I-RO (Internet Registration Office) at iros.go.kr, together with the StartBiz corporate startup portal for integrated name clearance and incorporation filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be in Hangul. A foreign-language name may be added in parentheses as an auxiliary name and must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul for the registered main name. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a Korean-language description of business purpose, (3) the legal-form suffix Chusik Hoesa, and (4) an optional English or other foreign-language parenthetical transliteration. An English-only primary name is not accepted for commercial registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The 30-day name reservation window is not automatically extensible; if the reservation expires, the applicant must refile through I-RO. If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant or legal counsel should request a written statement of rejection grounds within 14 days. Thereafter, the applicant may file an administrative appeal or objection with the competent district court registry, attaching evidence of dissimilarity, different business purpose, acquired distinctiveness, or written consent from the earlier registrant. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act or seek a judicial confirmation of the trade name in civil proceedings. All appeal submissions must be in Korean and supported by the original rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a clean outsourced virtual CFO company, Korea does not impose a specific head-count or capital commercial-substance test, but the National Tax Service and regulated banks demand a genuine management place. A serviced-office lease with a dedicated desk, physical signage, and mail handling is permissible; a post-office box or a bare virtual mailbox is not. The location must allow National Tax Service site confirmation under the Value-Added Tax Act and must be shown on the business registration certificate. Since the target payment rails include Stripe Billing and Wise, a local bank account and credible physical office presence will be required for onboarding; otherwise the risk of account closure or refusal is high.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) nameplate visible at the registered address; (2) valid lease of at least one year issued by a licensed serviced-office operator; (3) dedicated work surface, meeting room, and file storage; (4) management, client, and accounting records physically or digitally accessible at the address; (5) authorized representative reachable during posted business hours; (6) separate utility or business-center invoices; (7) ability to produce VAT invoices and statutory books to tax officers. Quantified risk: below 5% for a genuinely staffed serviced office in a commercial building in Seoul; 15% to 25% for a mail-forwarding virtual office; above 50% if the address is only a private mailbox or day-pass coworking space.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and preliminary name clearance request through I-RO and StartBiz
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee for the preliminary online name search; counsel time is billed within the legal due-diligence fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of Chusik Hoesa Articles of Association, corporate governance documents, and incorporation application package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean licensed external attorney or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed-fee market benchmark for a standard non-listed Chusik Hoesa with no mandatory minimum capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association and registered representative signatures before a Korean notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff based on the notarized amount and notarial public fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registration fee and local registration tax on incorporation (registration tax of 0.4% of capital, local education surtax of 20% of registration tax, and court registry fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent district court registry and local government
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariffs under the Registration Tax Act and the Court Fees Act; based on an assumed paid-in capital of KRW 100,000,000, with the final fee scaling by actual capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate and VAT registration under the Value-Added Tax Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee for corporate tax or VAT registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign parent document apostille and consular legalization bundle covering certificate of good standing, certificate of incorporation, board resolution, power of attorney, and bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary, foreign competent authority for Hague Apostille, and Korean consular section where consular legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government consular and legalization statutory fees plus prevailing notarial market rates; estimated at USD 70 per instrument for five instruments.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening database setup for all natural-person beneficial owners and directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial AML/CFT screening data vendor and compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark for single-entity onboarding with continuous monitoring for 12 months.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and commercial substance package in Seoul consisting of serviced office with physical nameplate, meeting room, and mail handling for six months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 400 per month for a compliance-grade virtual office, payable in advance for six months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Act No. 9746, as amended), Chapter IV 'Stock Companies': Articles 288-289 (establishment), 291 (contents of the Articles of Incorporation), 312-317 (election and registration of directors and statutory auditor), 317 (registration of incorporation), 421 (payment and deposit of subscription price), 431 (verification of payment by directors), and 542-2 (statutory auditor requirements), together with the Registration of Corporations Practice Rules issued by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The local Court Registry Office (Registration Division) of the Supreme Court of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company, operating through the Internet Registration Office portal of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Company (the incorporation registration application, with the notarized Articles of Incorporation attached as the primary constitutive instrument).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act; there is no statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, all subscribed shares must be fully paid up, and the paid-in capital must be deposited in a temporary incorporation deposit account opened in the name of the company at a licensed commercial bank in Korea. That account is effectively blocked and cannot be withdrawn until the incorporation registration is completed, after which the funds are released to the operating account of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE SUBSCRIBERS AND THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA. At the organizational meeting duly convened and held on ___ day of ______, 20___, at the proposed registered office of the Company in Korea, all subscribers to the shares of the Company and all persons designated as directors in the notarized Articles of Incorporation were present in person or by proxy. The meeting constituted a lawful quorum, notice was duly waived, and the following resolutions were adopted unanimously. 1. Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company is KRW [___] divided into [___] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [___] per share; that each subscriber subscribed for and fully paid in cash the number of shares set opposite his/her name in the subscription schedule; and that the paid-in capital deposit certificate issued by [Name of Korean Bank] is hereby ratified as conclusive evidence of full payment for purposes of Article 421 of the Commercial Act. 2. Adoption of Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted at [full municipal address in Korea] within the jurisdiction of the [___] Court Registry Office; and that the Representative Director is authorized to execute and deliver the office lease, registration consents, and any amendments or renewal documents necessary to preserve the administrative seat and legal address of the Company. 3. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the temporary incorporation deposit account maintained at the above-mentioned bank is hereby converted into the general operating account of the Company; and that the Representative Director, jointly with the Chief Financial Officer or jointly with the Statutory Auditor as required by bank mandate requirements, is authorized to open, operate, and close all bank accounts, including multicurrency accounts, merchant accounts, and payment platform accounts through Stripe Billing and Wise; to execute signature cards, KYC/AML declarations, foreign-exchange documents, and online banking mandates; and to set transaction limits. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED, that [Name] is hereby appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer with authority to represent the Company in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation; [Name] is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] is hereby appointed as initial Statutory Auditor, or if the Company is exempt from audit under applicable external audit law, as director without audit authority, in each case to hold office until the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders. 5. Licensing and Tax Registration. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director is authorized and directed to make all filings and registrations required to commence business, including the business registration certificate application with the National Tax Service, VAT registration, corporate seal registration, and the retention of licensed tax accountants or certified public accountants for any regulated bookkeeping, tax representation, or audit-related services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Korean name validation, and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company name validation through the Internet Registration Office managed by the Supreme Court of Korea; notarization before a licensed Korean notary public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English-translated Korean legal form containing the exact corporate name ending with Chusik Hoesa, principal office address, detailed corporate objects limited to virtual CFO advisory, fractional CFO services, management consulting, bookkeeping preparation, multicurrency ledger support, back-office and financial process outsourcing, and ancillary legal compliance support. Include share capital, number and par value of shares, public notice method, director and auditor clauses, and indemnity provisions. Search for name availability through the Internet Registration Office and, if available, execute the Articles of Incorporation before all subscribers. Have the executed Articles notarized by a Korean notary public. Non-resident subscribers must attach certified passports, power of attorney, and certified English/Korean translations for the local filing agent.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Subscriber identification documents and passports
Foreign investor certificate or alien registration card where applicable
Power of attorney appointing the Korean filing agent
Company name availability report from the Supreme Court registry portal
Proposed registered office address and lease if already secured
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the intended corporate name is rejected because it is identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name, select a distinctive alternative and repeat the name search and notarization process. No penalty is incurred as long as the correction is made before the incorporation registration application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the temporary incorporation deposit account and paid-in capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in Korea authorized to accept statutory incorporation deposits; for non-resident investors, the foreign exchange desk of the same bank operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation deposit account in the name of the company at a Korean bank. Complete the bank's application, AML/KYC, beneficial ownership, and source-of-funds forms. All subscribers must deposit the full subscription price stated in the Articles of Incorporation, but no statutory minimum is applicable. For non-resident subscribers, remit funds through lawful foreign-exchange channels and preserve the telegraphic transfer receipts. After all funds are credited, obtain from the bank a certificate of deposit of subscription price or an equivalent bank passbook/statement showing the full amount. The funds remain blocked for withdrawal until the Court Registry Office registers the incorporation; any early withdrawal would jeopardize the registration.
required_dossiers: Application form for temporary incorporation deposit account
Draft or notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscribers' passports or alien registration cards
Source of funds and bank reference documentation
Power of attorney for the local signor
AML/KYC and beneficial ownership declaration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence because of foreign ownership or source of funds, provide corporate organizational documents of the foreign parent, audited financial statements, references, and a certified translation of any constitutional documents. If the bank still withholds approval, engage an alternative licensed bank or escalate the file to the bank's financial crimes compliance committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory incorporation registration at the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The Court Registry Office under the Supreme Court of Korea, through the Internet Registration Office portal or by physical submission at the registry with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation within two weeks after all subscriptions and full payment have been completed. Submit the application for registration of establishment of a stock company together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of deposit of subscription price, the subscription schedule, consent/acceptance letters of directors and the statutory auditor, the organizational meeting records, the registration-tax payment receipt, and the corporate seal registration form. The registry will verify that all paid-in capital is blocked in the temporary account and that the directors and auditor have accepted their appointments. After approval, the registry issues a certificate of incorporation and a corporate registration number. Immediately thereafter, submit the corporate seal declaration to obtain a corporate seal certificate, which is required for subsequent tax and bank filings.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit of subscription price from the bank
Subscription schedule of shares signed by all subscribers
Written acceptance/consent letters of directors and auditor
Organizational meeting minutes or equivalent incorporator consent records
Power of attorney authorizing the local representative
Registration and license tax receipt
Corporate seal declaration and seal impression card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Court Registry issues a supplementary or correction order, comply within the statutory correction period by amending the Articles, supplying missing attachments, paying additional fees, or correcting the corporate seal record. If the application is suspended, review the registry's written reasons, rectify the specified defect, and resubmit. If the two-week filing deadline is missed and the application is rejected, reopen the deposit and repeat the payment and verification process before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration and tax enrollment with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea through the local branch tax office exercising jurisdiction over the registered office and through the HomeTax electronic tax portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file the application for a business registration certificate for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and employee withholding with the branch tax office. Complete the application to reflect the principal business as accounting and bookkeeping advisory services, using the fiscal classification corresponding to management consultancy and financial back-office outsourcing, and set the invoicing and VAT electronic bill issuance structure. Provide the corporate registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, registered-office lease, CEO identity, and power of attorney if filed by an agent. Obtain the business registration certificate with the corporate tax identification number and register for e-mailing electronic tax invoices. If the company will provide regulated bookkeeping or tax representation, simultaneously file the professional license or appointment record through the responsible certified tax accountant or certified public accountant.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal certificate
Business license application form from HomeTax
Registered lease or property use consent
CEO and authorized representative identification
Power of attorney for local tax agent
License certificates of any responsible tax accountant or certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service flags the application for additional verification, provide the actual office lease, utility bill, and photographs of the operational office, and submit the supplementary documents through HomeTax. A temporary tax registration number may be issued pending field verification; upon compliance the full business registration certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the corporate operating account and enabling multicurrency payment platforms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of the company's choice in Korea, operating under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with merchant integration through Stripe Billing and Wise.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the general operating and multicurrency current account at the bank. Submit the business registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, certification of incorporation, CEO identity, and a board resolution excerpt confirming authorized signatories and bank mandate. Complete beneficial ownership, AML/KYC, and target-market documentation for online services. After bank account activation, create the merchant entity with Stripe Billing and Wise using the legal company name, tax identification number, registered address, and Korean bank account details. Verify all directors and signatories on the payment platforms and configure multicurrency receiver accounts for foreign client invoicing. Ensure compliance with cross-border payment recordkeeping and any tax identification number disclosures under applicable tax treaties.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal certificate and seal impression certificate
Board resolution authorizing opening of bank accounts
Passports/IDs of authorized directors
Beneficial ownership declaration
Stripe Billing and Wise onboarding documents with tax IDs and bank details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment platform rejects the application due to foreign beneficial ownership or lack of local operating substance, submit a beneficial ownership chart, service contracts, a physical office lease, and a local employee or agent appointment letter. If KYC remains unsatisfactory, engage a licensed banking introducer or move to an alternative financial institution that accepts professional-services companies with foreign shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory licensing and professional credential validation for virtual CFO services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service for business license; Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants and Korean Association of Tax Professionals under the Ministry of Economy and Finance for professional credential matters; no industrial manufacturing licensing authority applies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review the exact scope of the company's service contracts. If the company will provide pure virtual CFO, fractional CFO, management advisory, cash-flow modeling, KPI reporting, and bookkeeping preparation only, no separate industrial or financial services license is required beyond the business registration certificate. If the company will prepare tax returns, sign tax declarations, or represent clients before tax authorities in Korea, at least one certified tax accountant registered with the Korean Association of Tax Professionals must be engaged. If the company will perform statutory audits or issue certified financial statements, the entity or the responsible practitioner must hold a certified public accountant license issued under the Certified Public Accountants Act. Document the internal compliance manual, client KYC files, outsourcing protocols, and data protection safeguards. Record all practitioner licenses in the company registry files and maintain client engagement records for regulatory inspection.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate
Professional licenses of responsible certified tax accountant or certified public accountant
CFO advisory service contract templates
Internal compliance and AML/KYC manual
Data protection and subcontracting procedures
Certificate of incorporation and corporate registry extracts
Office occupancy fire and safety record for the leased premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a regulator or a client questions whether the company is carrying on a regulated activity, obtain a scope-of-practice legal opinion from a Korean corporate attorney confirming that management advisory and fractional CFO services do not constitute audit, certified accounting, or tax representation. If the company inadvertently crosses into regulated territory, immediately retain a licensed certified tax accountant or certified public accountant and execute a retroactive engagement agreement before further deliverables are issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for ISIC 6920 as an industrial manufacturing authority; professional licensing oversight rests with the National Tax Service, the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants, and the Korean Association of Tax Professionals under the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate for the corporation under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Corporate Tax Act; if the company provides Korean tax return preparation or bookkeeping services as a regulated activity, the responsible practitioner must hold the Certified Tax Accountant license; if the company performs statutory audits or certified financial reports, the responsible practitioner must hold the Certified Public Accountant license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea; no EIA review is triggered for ISIC 6920 professional consultancy services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable: the enterprise is a virtual CFO advisory and bookkeeping services company with no fixed-source industrial emissions and no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable: zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero volatile organic compound stationary sources, and zero hazardous waste generation from service activities. The company must comply with general municipal solid waste disposal and commercial office waste separation rules; if office printing and general office waste are generated, they must be disposed of under local waste management service contracts. No environmental permit, water discharge permit, or air emissions permit is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial fire-permit enterprise. For the office-only operations, the lessor must provide a valid fire safety inspection and firefighting facilities maintenance certificate under the Firefighting Facilities Act. The company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for general administrative workplaces, including basic safety education and emergency evacuation planning; no factory, structural load, or civil defense site approval is required because the premises are used as a professional services office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea via the HomeTax electronic tax portal at hometax.go.kr; export declarations and customs supervision are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident entities may obtain a Korean Business Registration Number (BRN), which simultaneously serves as the corporate TIN and VAT registration number, before commencing taxable activities in Korea. For a foreign entity with a domestic place of business, registration is submitted to the district tax office having jurisdiction over that domestic business location using the HomeTax foreign-corporation business-registration service, accompanied by: certificate of incorporation or foreign registration certificate, constitutional documents, a board resolution documenting commencement of Korean business, proof of the domestic place of business, and a tax representative appointment where the entity does not maintain a principal office in Korea. A non-resident entity without any Korean establishment that supplies remote electronic services to Korean consumers may apply through the simplified foreign VAT registration route on HomeTax, including a foreign-user ID and password, the foreign entity registration certificate, and ratification of a Korean tax representative or VAT-dealing agent. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number after validation. Registration must be completed within 20 days from the start of Korean business, and no VAT invoice may be issued before the BRN is obtained. Any changes to the registered particulars must be reported within 15 days, and closure must be reported when Korean taxable activity ceases. Once registered, the entity files quarterly VAT returns and annual corporate income tax returns through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None of the U.S. check-the-box pass-through elections are available under Korean tax law; a Chusik Hoesa is a per-se entity-level taxpayer. Korean tax law permits qualifying wholly-owned domestic corporations to elect consolidated group taxation under the Corporate Tax Act when the statutory shareholding and business-preservation conditions are met. A foreign-incorporated entity whose head office or place of effective management is in Korea is statutorily classified as a domestic corporation, and hybrid-mismatch adjustments apply under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act and the Framework Act on International Taxation; these are not elective subclassification mechanisms. For this vehicle, available elections are therefore limited to consolidated filing eligibility and tax-year alignment, not entity pass-through status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration applies from the first taxable supply, without an economic de minimis for ordinary businesses, and business registration must be filed within 20 days of commencement. The Value-Added Tax Act provides a low-turnover exemption where prior-year taxable supplies do not exceed KRW 10,000,000; for foreign remote-digital-services suppliers, registration is required from the first deemed taxable Korean supply, and a simplified foreign VAT registration pathway is available for suppliers without a Korean place of business.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoicing through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system for all VAT-registered businesses. Tax invoices for B2B taxable supplies must be issued electronically and transmitted to the NTS via HomeTax or an authorised API integration, with the NTS-assigned electronic invoice serial number. B2C taxable sales are generally recorded through the electronic cash-receipt system, which transmits transaction data to the NTS database in near real time. Korea does not operate a transaction-level pre-clearance or physical digital-stamping fiscal server; anti-fraud control is implemented through mandatory electronic issuance, unique NTS invoice coding, real-time cash-receipt reporting, cross-matching of input and output VAT, and statutory penalties for false, delayed, or omitted invoices. Third-party billing and ERP providers may integrate with the NTS using the taxpayer's electronic certificate and API credentials.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT export rate applies to goods physically exported from Korea after an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, with export proceeds repatriated to Korea in convertible currency. Services, including B2B virtual CFO advisory, fractional CFO services, multicurrency bookkeeping, and qualifying offshore digital services, are zero-rated where the supply is made to a non-resident business or foreign consumer, the service is wholly or effectively used and consumed outside Korea, and the service is not connected to any Korean permanent establishment of the supplier. The zero-rating must be supported by contemporaneous evidence such as the export declaration, transport documents, service agreement, invoices, foreign payment receipts, and any record demonstrating offshore consumption; the burden of proof rests on the taxpayer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry equivalent) filed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS and endorsed with an Export Declaration Acceptance Number including HS code, quantity, FOB value, exporter and importer identifiers
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document showing the goods were consigned to the foreign buyer and physically removed from Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Korean Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation issued by a licensed bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, sales contract or purchase order, and internal collection schedule reconciled to the export declaration and transport document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without complete substantiation or where documentation is found to be false, the NTS may reopen the relevant tax period, disallow the zero rating, assess VAT at the standard 10% rate on the supply value, deny or claw back input VAT credits already refunded, and impose statutory understatement penalty tax and interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. Where fictitious export declarations, false invoices, or unverified foreign remittances are used, the Korea Customs Service and NTS may also impose customs penalties, initiate criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and seek fines or imprisonment. The clawback statute of limitations generally extends to ten years for fraudulent or unfiled returns and five years for understatements, and the taxpayer retains the full burden to prove actual export, foreign receipt, and offshore consumption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the supervisory framework of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a fundamentally liberal but surveillance-heavy foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions, including dividend remittances, royalties, and service fee payments, are fully convertible without licensing, provided that supporting documents and bank-issued tax/filing receipts are presented to a domestic foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions are subject to a registration or notification system: inbound equity investments of a non-resident into a Chusik Hoesa must be reported via the foreign exchange bank to the Minister of Economy and Finance for cross-border capital receipt purposes. The Korean won is freely convertible onshore for residents, but non-residents face restrictions on the external settlement of KRW without underlying economic activity. Profit remittance requires a certified tax clearance (corporate income tax return, local tax payment certificates) plus audited financial statements. There is no surrender requirement for export proceeds, but every foreign currency receipt must be credited to a domestic foreign currency deposit account or immediately converted to KRW, and all receipts are reported electronically to the customs service through the foreign exchange information system. Administrative penalties apply for unreported inward remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect proceeds within six months from the export date, extendable upon application to the head of the relevant domestic bank, and must either deposit the foreign currency in an authorized foreign currency deposit account or convert to KRW at a domestic foreign exchange bank; no fixed statutory conversion ratio exists, but full repatriation and electronic notification to the Korea Customs Service (Foreign Exchange Information System) are mandatory for each transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Operational Settlement Account with integrated foreign currency deposit sub-ledger
Capital Escrow/Reception Account for Paid-in Capital and Foreign Equity Injection
Multicurrency Current Account for Subscription Payments and Trade Settlement
Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account (USD/EUR/JPY) with FX Forward Authorization

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and Stripe are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission as 'electronic financial business operators' for the purpose of operating domestic won-denominated virtual accounts. A Korean-incorporated Chusik Hoesa must route all inbound FX receipts through a domestically registered foreign exchange bank and file electronic reports via the Foreign Exchange Information System. An offshore EMI can be used only as a supplementary payment acceptance terminal (for example, Stripe Billing as a SaaS billing processor) provided that all settlement amounts are ultimately swept to a Korean foreign exchange bank account in the name of the same legal entity; however, the EMI will not be recognized as a clearing bank for statutory capital verification, profit remittance, or tax clearance purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes, the statutory representative (CEO inside the Chusik Hoesa) must appear personally in the relevant bank branch for account-opening verification. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by the major commercial banks for a resident-incorporated entity with non-resident shareholders; the bank's compliance committee requires physical proof of principal identity, business purpose, and beneficial ownership attestation at the initial underwriting stage. If the director is a foreign national residing overseas, a notarized and apostilled power of attorney executed under Korea's Act on Notarial Acts may allow a local resident agent to attend process, but the bank still requires the physical appearance of at least one executive officer who passes fingerprint/biometric verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent cross-border client base and large ticket subscription invoices without granular transactional narrative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhance with a full client contract registry, signed engagement letters per vendor, invoice-level billing descriptions, records of the underlying service delivery (time sheets, deliverables, email correspondence), three prior months of domestic payroll and subclass tax (VAT 10%) filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder chain with multiple intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide apostilled or superlegalized certificates of incorporation and articles of association for each holding layer, a certified final beneficiary economic ownership schedule, passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owners, sworn source-of-funds statements, and bank-issued confirmation from the originating offshore bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual volume of same-day round-trip flows between the Korea operational account and a foreign exchange swap account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present pre-approval of the FX hedging programme from the bank's Treasury Advisory Desk, unaudited quarterly management accounts showing genuine operational liquidity, executed forward contracts with ISDA-style double-party confirmation, and booking records that map each outward/receiving cycle to specific client trades.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Clients located in high-risk jurisdictions or sensitive industries (online gaming, digital content)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver sanctions screening results from a respected compliance platform for every counterparty, export/ACE compliance certificates for digital content, enhanced due diligence files locating beneficial owners, source-of-wealth, local tax registration, and application of reliable corporate KYC tools; for gaming clients, include a self-exclusion and AML programme certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity contributions from a non-resident shareholder must be credited to the company's foreign currency deposit account at a designated foreign exchange bank with the applicable capital contribution receipt purpose code, and the bank submits an automated report to the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The capital appraisal certificate (shareholder capital verification statement) is then issued by the bank upon receipt of the funds, after which the amount may be converted into KRW for operating liquidity. For amounts exceeding USD 50,000, the remitting bank must obtain the company's tax registration certificate and the shareholder's equity distribution plan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border service payments (e.g., subcontract fees, marketing expenses) are settled by SWIFT MT103 with the mandatory payment purpose code for service income, whereas the import of physical goods or integrated software licensing could be covered by documentary collection (CAD/DP) or an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC). All outbound payments pass the bank's automated FX validation, and each disbursement must be backed by an underlying invoice, contract, and for amounts above the threshold, the tax invoice for VAT purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD spot and forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank up to 12 months tenor
Cross-currency swaps for repayment of overseas borrowings
FX options and structured options (vanilla call/collar) with a notional directly tied to contractual export or settlement exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore for Korean-domiciled legal entities except under explicit regulatory approval, and participation in the offshore NDF market is restricted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local income tax surcharge declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (HomeTax electronic filing) and the relevant local government for the local income tax surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due March 31; extension allowed when the return is prepared and certified by a professional tax preparer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing addition of 20% of tax due, unfaithful-return penalty of 10% of understated tax, statutory daily delinquency interest, collection measures and possible business license suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and shareholders; corporate records retained at the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fine up to KRW 10,000,000 imposed on directors for failure to convene the regular general meeting; directors jointly liable for losses caused by unlawful distributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be completed before the annual general meeting and submitted to the Financial Services Commission within 14 days after the general meeting for entities subject to mandatory external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and criminal sanctions for failure to appoint an auditor or to file the audit report; false audit reports expose the company and the external auditor to regulatory penalties and investor damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of member register, director register and beneficial ownership records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records; no standalone annual government UBO filing for a private Chusik Hoesa unless a reportable foreign investment transaction occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register review completed before the annual general meeting; member register updated upon each share transfer or issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Act fines for inaccurate register entries; company cannot assert unrecorded share transfers against bona fide transferees; foreign-exchange-related reporting omissions trigger penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: External audit is mandatory under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies when total assets at fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) or when the company meets the additional size, revenue and employment criteria set by Presidential Decree; listed companies, financial institutions and public-interest companies are subject to audit regardless of asset size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS is required for listed companies and financial institutions; a non-listed Chusik Hoesa may apply K-IFRS voluntarily or use Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) under the business accounting standards approved by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants; corporate taxable income is reconciled to accounting income under the Corporate Income Tax Act

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO filing for a private Chusik Hoesa. The company must annually verify the member register and director holdings at the board and general meeting. A beneficial ownership confirmation identifying the natural persons exercising ultimate control through shareholding or other means should be prepared and recorded in minutes. Reportable foreign share acquisitions and changes must be declared to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 900 per year for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 per year for a small non-audit-tier Chusik Hoesa; larger mandatory audits range from USD 10,000 to USD 50,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (highest bracket for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion) plus 10% local income tax surcharge, yielding a combined top effective rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Special Tax Control Act: SME job-creation credits up to 25%; R&D expense credits of 10%–20%; tax holidays/credits in Free Economic Zones; for a virtual CFO/accounting business, such credits depend on domestic employment and qualifying tangible/R&D investments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Seoul National Tax Service (NTS) Hometax system – Standard Corporate Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서) Form No. 101, plus attached Local Income Tax Return (지방소득세 신고서).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, filing deadline is March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from virtual CFO advisory, bookkeeping, and consulting services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross revenue accrued to the Korean entity, irrespective of shareholder residency; translate foreign-currency receipts using the fiscal-year-end BOK basic exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (personnel, software, subcontracting, office rent, depreciation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only arms-length business expenses supported by tax invoices (세금계산서), credit-card receipts, and written contracts; disallow costs paid to non-resident affiliated persons without substantive benefit.
Reconcile Korean IFRS/K-GAAP accounting income with corporate tax adjustments; enter the audited profit of the Korean legal entity, not the consolidated result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base (과세표준) after non-taxable income and non-deductible expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back prior-year losses in excess of statutory carryforward, entertainment expenses exceeding limits, and deemed staffing costs; subtract tax-exempt income only when supported by law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional corporate tax computed at progressive rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the bracket rates separately: 9% for the first KRW 200 million; 19% for KRW 200m–20bn; 21% for KRW 20bn–300bn; 24% above KRW 300bn.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax liability after credits, prepayments, and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct advance payment installments made during the year, foreign tax credits, and eligible tax credits; non-resident ownership does not automatically alter the final tax computation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of the unpaid corporate tax and, if over one month late, an additional 0.022% of unpaid tax per day; negligent underreporting: 10%–20% of the omitted amount; intentional underreporting: 30%–40% of the omitted amount; separate local income tax surcharge of up to 10% plus coercive collection and criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on gross dividend paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, plus 2% local income tax surcharge (10% of the national tax), for an effective statutory aggregate rate of 22%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Agreement (DTA) dividend rate, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Korean payer (a) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority, and (b) a completed NTS Form 'Application for Exemption from/Reduced Withholding Tax' (외국법인 원천징수특례 신청서). The Korean company then withholds at the treaty rate; if treaty relief is not secured before dividend distribution, the 22% must be withheld and the non-resident may apply to the District Tax Office for a refund after the tax year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest to non-residents: 20% national withholding + 2% local surcharge (effective 22%); royalty/technical services: 20% + 2% local surcharge (effective 22%). Under many Korean DTAs, treaty-restricted rates are commonly 10%–15% for interest and 10%–15% for royalties, subject to submission of the TRC and activation through the NTS reduced-withholding protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File under Article 13-1 of the International Tax Adjustment Act apply when cross-border transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 10 billion in the fiscal year; a lower KRW 5 billion threshold triggers the annual transfer-pricing summary report requirement.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the substance-over-form principle under the International Tax Adjustment Act GAAR and Korean Civil/Commercial law requires real business premises, employees, decision-making, and core services in Korea. A shell Chusik Hoesa lacking economic substance may be disregarded for tax purposes, denied treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test, or recharacterized by the NTS under anti-avoidance provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing virtual CFO consulting fees received through Stripe, Wise, or foreign bank accounts directly to non-resident owners without recording the revenue in the Korean entity's books, failing to issue tax invoices, and omitting the income from the annual corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine equal to up to 3 times the evaded tax; additional corporate income tax of 30% of the unreported amount plus daily late payment interest (0.022%); local income tax surcharge of 20%–30%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who concealed revenue or directed the use of foreign payment rails may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax penalty; the NTS can order a travel ban, initiate criminal indictment without prior administrative collection, and request seizure of personal assets; a court may pierce the corporate veil if the legal entity is found to be a mere instrument of the non-resident owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming or maintaining the Chusik Hoesa with no physical office, no local employees, no board meetings in Korea, and no substantive business activity, while seeking DTA relief on dividends and royalties repatriated to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the Korean GAAR under Article 14 of the International Tax Adjustment Act to recharacterize the Korean entity as a flow-through; denial of treaty benefits and reclassification of all foreign-source income as Korean taxable income; additional tax of up to 40% of the underreported corporate tax and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors appointed solely to mark compliance but without actual authority face personal civil restitution for any resulting tax shortfall; serious cases trigger criminal fraud charges, disqualification from serving as directors, and travel bans pending criminal or administrative proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit the Master File, Local File, or transfer-pricing summary report when related-party cross-border transactions exceed the statutory threshold, or submitting manipulated intercompany service agreements showing mark-ups well below arm's length without benchmarking studies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 5% of the aggregate transaction value for each missing required document; the NTS may disregard the submitted price, adjust taxable income to the arm's length result, and impose up to 30% additional tax on intentionally incorrect reporting; unpaid corporate tax also accrues daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false transfer-pricing records are personally liable for penalties arising from fraud; in aggravated cases, criminal charges for obstruction of tax investigation carry imprisonment, and the court may impose personal recovery orders against company assets and directors' remuneration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a virtual CFO service provider without conducting customer identification, beneficial-owner verification, or suspicious-transaction reporting while receiving high-volume fees through digital payment platforms (Stripe, Wise) from ambiguous client funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Transaction Reports Act: fines up to KRW 100 million for failure to report suspicious transactions or establish AML controls; the National Tax Service may additionally disallow deductions and impose penalties for unfounded cash receipts; the regulatory body may revoke the statutory accounting-service license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal liability if the control failure was deliberate; penalties include imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to KRW 30 million; the company's civil liability for sanctions may be assigned to directors on grounds of gross managerial negligence.
